comc-2012-a1.prompt: Determine the positive integer $n$ such that $8^4 = 4^n$.

comc-2012-a2.prompt: Let $x$ be the average of the following six numbers: $\{12, 412, 812, 1212, 1612, 2012\}$. Determine the value of $x$.

comc-2012-a3.prompt: Let $ABCDEF$ be a hexagon all of whose sides are equal in length and all of whose angles are equal. The area of hexagon $ABCDEF$ is exactly $r$ times the area of triangle $ACD$. Determine the value of $r$.

comc-2012-a4.prompt: Twelve different lines are drawn on the coordinate plane so that each line is parallel to exactly two other lines. Furthermore, no three lines intersect at a point. Determine the total number of intersection points among the twelve lines.

comc-2012-b1.prompt:
Alice and Bob run in the clockwise direction around a circular track, each running at a constant speed. Alice can complete a lap in $t$ seconds, and Bob can complete a lap in $60$ seconds. They start at diametrically-opposite points.

When they meet for the first time, Alice has completed exactly $30$ laps. Determine all possible values of $t$.

comc-2012-b2.prompt:
For each positive integer $n$, define $\varphi(n)$ to be the number of positive divisors of $n$. For example, $\varphi(10) = 4$, since $10$ has $4$ positive divisors, namely $\{1, 2, 5, 10\}$.

Suppose $n$ is a positive integer such that $\varphi(2n) = 6$. Determine the minimum possible value of $\varphi(6n)$.

comc-2012-b3.prompt:
Given the following $4$ by $4$ square grid of points, determine the number of ways we can label ten different points $A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, J$ such that the lengths of the nine segments
$$AB,\ BC,\ CD,\ DE,\ EF,\ FG,\ GH,\ HI,\ IJ$$
are in strictly increasing order.

comc-2012-b4.prompt: In the following diagram, two lines that meet at a point $A$ are tangent to a circle at points $B$ and $C$. The line parallel to $AC$ passing through $B$ meets the circle again at $D$. Join the segments $CD$ and $AD$. Suppose $AB = 49$ and $CD = 28$. The length of $AD$ is a positive integer $n$. Determine $n$.

comc-2012-c1a.prompt:
Let $f(x) = x^2$ and $g(x) = 3x - 8$.

(a) Determine the values of $f(2)$ and $g(f(2))$.

comc-2012-c1b.prompt:
Let $f(x) = x^2$ and $g(x) = 3x - 8$.

(b) Determine all values of $x$ such that $f(g(x)) = g(f(x))$.

comc-2012-c1c.prompt:
Let $f(x) = x^2$ and $g(x) = 3x - 8$.

(c) Let $h(x) = 3x - r$. Determine all values of $r$ such that $f(h(2)) = h(f(2))$.

comc-2012-c2a.prompt:
We fill a $3 \times 3$ grid with 0s and 1s. We score one point for each row, column, and diagonal whose sum is odd.

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline 1 & 1 & 0 \\ \hline 1 & 0 & 1 \\ \hline 0 & 1 & 1 \\ \hline\end{array} \qquad\qquad \begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline 1 & 1 & 1 \\ \hline 1 & 0 & 1 \\ \hline 0 & 1 & 1 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

For example, the grid on the left has $0$ points and the grid on the right has $3$ points.

(a) Fill in a grid so that the grid has exactly $1$ point. Many answers are possible; you only need to provide one.
comc-2012-c2a.answer: e.g. rows $101$, $110$, $011$ (only the main diagonal $1+1+1$ is odd)

comc-2012-c2b.prompt:
We fill a $3 \times 3$ grid with 0s and 1s. We score one point for each row, column, and diagonal whose sum is odd.

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline 1 & 1 & 0 \\ \hline 1 & 0 & 1 \\ \hline 0 & 1 & 1 \\ \hline\end{array} \qquad\qquad \begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline 1 & 1 & 1 \\ \hline 1 & 0 & 1 \\ \hline 0 & 1 & 1 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

For example, the grid on the left has $0$ points and the grid on the right has $3$ points.

(b) Determine all grids with exactly $8$ points.

comc-2012-c2c.prompt:
We fill a $3 \times 3$ grid with 0s and 1s. We score one point for each row, column, and diagonal whose sum is odd.

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline 1 & 1 & 0 \\ \hline 1 & 0 & 1 \\ \hline 0 & 1 & 1 \\ \hline\end{array} \qquad\qquad \begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline 1 & 1 & 1 \\ \hline 1 & 0 & 1 \\ \hline 0 & 1 & 1 \\ \hline\end{array}$$

For example, the grid on the left has $0$ points and the grid on the right has $3$ points.

(c) Let $E$ be the number of grids with an even number of points, and $O$ be the number of grids with an odd number of points. Prove that $E = O$.
comc-2012-c2c.answer: Pair each grid with the grid obtained by switching the top-left entry: this flips the parity of exactly $3$ lines, so it changes the parity of the score.

comc-2012-c3a.prompt:
Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram. We draw in the diagonal $AC$. A circle is drawn inside $\triangle ABC$ tangent to all three sides and touches side $AC$ at a point $P$.

(a) Prove that $DA + AP = DC + CP$.
comc-2012-c3a.answer: Equal tangents: $AP = AB - BX$, $CP = CB - BY$ with $BX = BY$, and $DA = CB$, $DC = AB$.

comc-2012-c3b.prompt:
Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram. We draw in the diagonal $AC$. A circle is drawn inside $\triangle ABC$ tangent to all three sides and touches side $AC$ at a point $P$.

(b) Draw in the line $DP$. A circle of radius $r_1$ is drawn inside $\triangle DAP$ tangent to all three sides. A circle of radius $r_2$ is drawn inside $\triangle DCP$ tangent to all three sides. Prove that
$$\frac{r_1}{r_2} = \frac{AP}{PC}.$$
comc-2012-c3b.answer: Area $= r \cdot s$ for each triangle; $\triangle DAP$ and $\triangle DCP$ have equal perimeters by (a) and share the height from $D$.

comc-2012-c3c.prompt:
Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram. We draw in the diagonal $AC$. A circle is drawn inside $\triangle ABC$ tangent to all three sides and touches side $AC$ at a point $P$.

Draw in the line $DP$. A circle of radius $r_1$ is drawn inside $\triangle DAP$ tangent to all three sides, and a circle of radius $r_2$ is drawn inside $\triangle DCP$ tangent to all three sides. (It can be shown that $DA + AP = DC + CP$ and $\frac{r_1}{r_2} = \frac{AP}{PC}$.)

(c) Suppose $DA + DC = 3AC$ and $DA = DP$. Determine the ratio $r_1/r_2$.

comc-2012-c4a.prompt:
For any positive integer $n$, an $n$-tuple of positive integers $(x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n)$ is said to be *super-squared* if it satisfies both of the following properties:

(1) $x_1 > x_2 > x_3 > \cdots > x_n$.

(2) The sum $x_1^2 + x_2^2 + \cdots + x_k^2$ is a perfect square for each $1 \le k \le n$.

For example, $(12, 9, 8)$ is super-squared, since $12 > 9 > 8$, and each of $12^2$, $12^2 + 9^2$, and $12^2 + 9^2 + 8^2$ are perfect squares.

(a) Determine all values of $t$ such that $(32, t, 9)$ is super-squared.

comc-2012-c4b.prompt:
For any positive integer $n$, an $n$-tuple of positive integers $(x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n)$ is said to be *super-squared* if it satisfies both of the following properties:

(1) $x_1 > x_2 > x_3 > \cdots > x_n$.

(2) The sum $x_1^2 + x_2^2 + \cdots + x_k^2$ is a perfect square for each $1 \le k \le n$.

For example, $(12, 9, 8)$ is super-squared, since $12 > 9 > 8$, and each of $12^2$, $12^2 + 9^2$, and $12^2 + 9^2 + 8^2$ are perfect squares.

(b) Determine a super-squared $4$-tuple $(x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4)$ with $x_1 < 200$.

comc-2012-c4c.prompt:
For any positive integer $n$, an $n$-tuple of positive integers $(x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n)$ is said to be *super-squared* if it satisfies both of the following properties:

(1) $x_1 > x_2 > x_3 > \cdots > x_n$.

(2) The sum $x_1^2 + x_2^2 + \cdots + x_k^2$ is a perfect square for each $1 \le k \le n$.

For example, $(12, 9, 8)$ is super-squared, since $12 > 9 > 8$, and each of $12^2$, $12^2 + 9^2$, and $12^2 + 9^2 + 8^2$ are perfect squares.

(c) Determine whether there exists a super-squared $2012$-tuple.
comc-2012-c4c.answer: Yes — by induction, any super-squared $k$-tuple with total $r^2$ can be scaled by $a$ and extended by $br$, where $(a, b, c)$ is a Pythagorean triple with $a/b > r/x_k$ (e.g. $(m^2-1, 2m, m^2+1)$ for large $m$).
